brief: Goldman's Cullen Morgan documents hedge-fund conviction shrinking further even as the S&P sits near highs and the Nasdaq makes new ones. Prime Brokerage data show US fundamental L/S net leverage falling a third straight week to 46.4% (2nd percentile, 5yr) while gross stays near 209% (79th percentile): funds hold size but go market-neutral. Goldman's Sentiment Indicator posted a fifth straight negative reading and non-dealers dumped $68bn of S&P futures over six weeks. The driver is partly the Fed: Goldman's Monetary Policy Optimism factor sits near a record low, the long end stayed bidless, and a soft 29K payrolls print gave only brief relief. Equity vol (Vol Panic Index 1.82/10) stays calm because the fear moved to credit, where the VVIX/HYG ratio hit a 3+ year low; Morgan reads this as the market not pricing spillover and calls VIX convexity cheap, while JPMorgan's Saul Doctor calls the credit widening a contrarian buy. Only tech got bought in September. Iran remains the largest overhang, with both banks positioned for a deal via QQQ-side calls. Consensus still expects 27% y/y Q3 EPS growth, concentrated in the top 10 names.
